column2: survey_text

Manual software development, even with excellent methodologies, cannot be more than about 15 percent better than average development, due to intrinsic limits on human performance and legal limits on working hours without fatigue.
The cost of breaching a system's security should be greater than the value of the assets it protects.
Some known software durability issues go unaddressed during development because of time constraints or other project pressures.
Projects that run late and have significant cost overruns are primarily caused by excessive defects that are not discovered or removed until testing begins.
The attack surface of an application is usually larger than a typical developer or software architect imagines.
A lack of an integrated build process makes deployment planning significantly harder and delays production deployment schedules.
When software quality improves and frees up personnel, the best use of that capacity for commercial software companies is expanding into new types of software and taking on more projects per year.
All infrastructure changes should go through a formal change management process and be deployed using Infrastructure as Code tools, so environments can be torn down and rebuilt quickly.
Establishing effective online forums allows developers and users to discuss specific usability issues related to the software.
Motivating team members through example and leadership is more effective than motivating them through hierarchical authority.
Quality is an essential aspect of software that contributes to its long-term durability.
Most companies focus primarily on faster development and set deadlines without properly estimating software durability.

Organizations adopting static application security testing (SAST) tools should have dedicated staff within Scrum teams responsible for this work, appoint security champions to liaise with the security team, and ensure enough security staff are available to train developers on secure development practices and proper tool use.
Functionality remains the key factor in determining a product's success.
Improving quality assurance can be a simple process based on common sense and a straightforward logical approach to fulfilling software engineering responsibilities.
Testing on its own, without pretest defect removal, is expensive and rarely exceeds 85 percent in defect removal efficiency.
Testing tools that link requirements to test cases typically do so by connecting requirement IDs with test IDs.
Drawing a diagram of linked, sequentially timed events and their causal relationships helps demonstrate how an incident occurred.
Organizations that sell software often want to limit the use of specific free and open source software (FOSS) licenses in their environment.
A domain analysis should describe how the current application works, including any existing software used to support it.
After initial development, software applications continue to grow in size by roughly 8 percent per year.
Software or code inspection should not be confused with code review or walkthrough, which is typically completed in a single meeting lasting a couple of hours.
Coding standards should not be adopted partway through a project.
Quality Assurance activities ensure that software products and processes meet defined quality standards.
Making discipline a habit helps software team members meet the knowledge and skill expectations set by management.
Cost per defect increases as software quality improves, which contradicts the assumptions behind standard economic measures of quality.
Functions that restrict a value to a fixed set of valid options should be tested with both valid and invalid inputs to confirm the restriction works.
Only about 20 percent of design code is typically reused in practice, well below an ideal reuse rate of around 75 percent.
Production rate is often paired with assignment scope to produce software cost and schedule estimates for specific activities.
Bad-fix injection rates, defects introduced while fixing other defects, are often higher than 20 percent when modifying high-complexity applications.
Using automated testing frameworks integrated into a CI/CD pipeline enables efficient and reliable test execution on every code commit.
Large software projects are frequently canceled, and most run late and exceed their budgets.
Trustworthiness is always a key factor in software usability and durability.
About 95 percent of the API endpoints used in data science work are GET and POST requests.
Leaving hooks in code for possible future use leads to testing anomalies and possible unreachable code.
Software applications must meet durability criteria to be successful.
It is technically possible to build some software applications from standard, reusable components.
Licensing issues need to be well understood and managed when using open source software in an end product.
The rise of platform as a service (PaaS) hosting may reduce or eliminate the need for a professional developer to be involved in deployment.
As software quality improves, cost per defect rises sharply.
Product owners and Scrum masters should plan for and allocate time and budget to ensure security and resilience constraints are included in design work.
Defects should be prevented from occurring in the first place.
Defect removal efficiency ranges from as high as 99.65 percent to as low as under 77 percent.
Teams should select only the metrics most relevant to their own product and market, rather than industry-wide standard metrics, and automate them to make adoption easier under time constraints.
Teams should ask for help resolving difficult problems and respond to issues quickly.
Defects should be resolved before exiting the current development phase or releasing to production.
Security, privacy, and durability solutions must be continually developed to remain effective.
Testers should ensure that code changes do not introduce new flaws into existing functionality.
A dedicated discussion forum allows team members to discuss project-related questions and suggestions separately from personal email.
Security awareness enables smoother engagement in software security education and sustained involvement in application security activities throughout the year.
